newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha contango vanishes, LSWR remains firm.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha contango vanishes, LSWR remains firm.

text.p: The contango in near-term naphtha spreads almost disappeared in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday, with the first-half September contract valued even with the second half of the month, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha was quoted at $200.50/$201.50 per tonne for both first-half and second-half of September.
Inter-delivery spreads had remained in contango since mid-April reflecting ample availability for prompt cargoes.
Traders said the spread movement goes against supply/demand fundamentals. There still are plenty of near-term cargoes in the region, they said.
A continuing heatwave in Tokyo and neighbouring regions continued to buttress sentiment in the low sulphur fuel oil market, traders said.
In Japan, operations of oil-fired thermal power plants, used as a buffer against fluctuations in power demand, usually peak in the summer as more people turn on air conditioners.
Temperatures in Tokyo exceeded 30 degrees Celsius for the seventh consecutive day on Wednesday.
Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc's (TEPCO) electricity output hit a maximum 55.6 million kilowatt (kw) in early afternoon, compared with 48.7 million kw a week ago.
